blockers.reason: NonCommercial restriction (Section 2(a)(1)) and ShareAlike copyleft (Section 3(b)) make this incompatible with commercial composite software stack. Not OSI-approved.
Strong network copyleft (AGPL Section 13) requires source disclosure for any network-accessible deployment. Core engine is AGPL despite MIT-licensed SDKs.
Strong network copyleft (AGPL Section 13) mandates corresponding source offer to remote users. Incompatible with proprietary/commercial distributions.
Strong copyleft; no LICENSE file in repo; bundles MIT-derived JS evasion scripts from puppeteer-extra-plugin-stealth creating mixed-source ambiguity.

missingEvidence.issue: No license text file (LICENSE, COPYING, NOTICE) exists in repository or git history. pyproject.toml declares MIT but README links to non-existent LICENSE file. Metadata declaration alone is insufficient per evidence standard.

package.json declares MIT but no LICENSE, COPYING, or NOTICE file exists in repo (confirmed via filesystem search, git ls-files, GitHub API 404). Runtime dependencies @browserbasehq/sdk and playwright are Apache-2.0 requiring additional obligations.
No LICENSE/COPYING/NOTICE text file in repository tree or git history. Only license declaration is SPDX string in pyproject.toml. Bundles MIT-derived evasion scripts without license text.

limitations: Dependency-level licenses (transitive dependencies of each repo) were not exhaustively audited; only repository-level license declarations and primary license files were evaluated.
Submodule/vendored code licenses were only partially verified (e.g., rapidfuzz C++ submodules not checked out, playwright-stealth evasion scripts provenance noted but not fully re-audited).

For repos with dual/multi-license structures (meilisearch, traceroot, firecrawl), the determination reflects the most restrictive applicable license for the core integration component; SDK/client sub-components may carry more permissive terms.
autoheal-locator-python is marked UNKNOWN because no license file exists anywhere in the repo or its history; the pyproject.toml classifier is treated as metadata, not primary evidence.

stagehand-agent is marked REVIEW (not UNKNOWN) because package.json declares MIT and upstream stagehand is MIT, but absence of a license file plus Apache-2.0 transitive dependencies creates a compliance gap requiring human legal review.
OSI-approval status was determined from the SPDX identifier and the OSI approved-licenses list; CC0-1.0, CC-BY-4.0, BUSL-1.1, CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 are not OSI-approved.
